newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares galloped higher in late session to set new intraday and closing highs.
"It's pretty simple: up, up and up we go," said one trader caught by the late bullish mood.

Other bourses, notably the British stock market, provided a hearty afternoon shove, but the Dutch market had some life of its own with ABN AMRO's announcement late on Friday of a takeover of a U.S. bank.
The AEX index closed 7.23 points, or 1.19 percent, higher at 615.47, just shy of a new all-time peak of 615.75 set in the last half hour of trading.

A day after ING announced a 24 percent rise in its net profits for the first nine months, ABN AMRO stole the limelight from its rival by saying it planned to take over Standard Federal Bank. The acquisition of the largest savings bank in the U.S. Mid West will ABN AMRO's biggest to date, the company said.
"In principle I applaud the move. It's in line with ABN AMRO's strategy of international expansion," said Jacob Bosscha, an analyst at Bank Labouchere.
ABN AMRO shares closed up 4.40 guilders to 109.70.
On Thursday, a number of chartists were bearish regarding the prospects for a push beyond the 610-615 range.
A rising dollar helped push up another multinational Philips. Its shares rose by 2.80 guilders to 64.60.
